headline: LP gas prices for July to be announced today in Bangladesh
summary: The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) is set to announce the adjusted prices for Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) for the month of July. This decision will impact household and commercial consumers nationwide.
details: The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) is scheduled to announce the new prices for Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) for the month of July today. This highly anticipated decision will determine whether consumers will face higher or lower costs for cooking and other uses.

LPG prices are adjusted monthly based on international market rates, the value of the US dollar against the Taka, and other operational costs. These adjustments directly affect millions of households and businesses across the country.
The BERC holds regular public hearings and consultations with stakeholders before finalizing the price structure. The aim is to ensure fair pricing while reflecting global market dynamics.

Consumers are closely watching the announcement, as even minor fluctuations in LPG prices can significantly impact household budgets. Previous months have seen varying trends, adding to the anticipation for July's rates.
caption:
Consumers across Bangladesh await today's crucial announcement on July's LPG prices. Will costs rise or fall?

The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) is scheduled to announce the new prices for Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) for the month of July today. This highly anticipated decision will determine whether consumers will face higher or lower costs for cooking and other uses.

LPG prices are adjusted monthly based on international market rates, the value of the US dollar against the Taka, and other operational costs. These adjustments directly affect millions of households and businesses across the country.

The BERC holds regular public hearings and consultations with stakeholders before finalizing the price structure. The aim is to ensure fair pricing while reflecting global market dynamics.

Consumers are closely watching the announcement, as even minor fluctuations in LPG prices can significantly impact household budgets. Previous months have seen varying trends, adding to the anticipation for July's rates.

headline: US signs deal with Israel for permanent Jerusalem embassy amid controversy
summary: The agreement, signed at Israel's Foreign Ministry, follows former President Trump's 2017 recognition of Jerusalem as Israel's capital and the relocation of the US embassy from Tel Aviv.
details: The United States and Israel have signed an agreement to construct a new, permanent embassy building in Jerusalem. The signing ceremony took place at Israel's Foreign Ministry on Wednesday.

This initiative follows former US President Donald Trump's 2017 decision to recognize Jerusalem as Israel's capital. Trump had also ordered the relocation of the US embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem at that time.

US Ambassador to Israel, Mike Hacaby, stated at the ceremony that Washington recognizes Jerusalem as the eternal capital of the Jewish people. He added that the new building would be a permanent and complete embassy, serving as the main hub for all US diplomatic activities in Israel.
Israeli Foreign Minister Gidon Sar welcomed the US initiative, asserting that the agreement further strengthens the "unbreakable friendship" between the two nations.
The new US embassy is slated for construction in an area known as the 'Allenby Compound', located in southern Jerusalem.
Jerusalem remains a central point of contention in the long-standing Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Palestinians claim East Jerusalem as the capital of their future independent state.

The Israeli human rights organization 'Adalah' has strongly condemned the construction of the US embassy in this disputed area. In a statement, the organization said the move "perpetuates a deep and historic injustice."
Adalah further highlighted that the land designated for the embassy was originally owned by Palestinians. It was forcibly confiscated by Israel under the discriminatory 1950 'Absentees' Property Law.
caption:

The United States and Israel have signed an agreement to construct a new, permanent embassy building in Jerusalem. The signing ceremony took place at Israel's Foreign Ministry on Wednesday.

This initiative follows former US President Donald Trump's 2017 decision to recognize Jerusalem as Israel's capital. Trump had also ordered the relocation of the US embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem at that time.

US Ambassador to Israel, Mike Hacaby, stated at the ceremony that Washington recognizes Jerusalem as the eternal capital of the Jewish people. He added that the new building would be a permanent and complete embassy, serving as the main hub for all US diplomatic activities in Israel.

Israeli Foreign Minister Gidon Sar welcomed the US initiative, asserting that the agreement further strengthens the "unbreakable friendship" between the two nations.

The new US embassy is slated for construction in an area known as the 'Allenby Compound', located in southern Jerusalem.

Jerusalem remains a central point of contention in the long-standing Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Palestinians claim East Jerusalem as the capital of their future independent state.

The Israeli human rights organization 'Adalah' has strongly condemned the construction of the US embassy in this disputed area. In a statement, the organization said the move "perpetuates a deep and historic injustice."

Adalah further highlighted that the land designated for the embassy was originally owned by Palestinians. It was forcibly confiscated by Israel under the discriminatory 1950 'Absentees' Property Law.
